SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Facility: Larkspur Valley Endoscopy Center (fictional)
Patient: Marian Quell (fictional)
Date of service: November 3, 2026
Endoscopist: Helena Marsh, MD (fictional)
Indication: Surveillance of a polypectomy scar in the ascending colon.
History: Piecemeal endoscopic mucosal resection of a 25 mm ascending colon polyp in May 2026.
Procedure: The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice.
Bowel preparation was good.
Findings:
- Ascending colon: a pale, stellate, well-healed scar at the prior resection site.
- The scar was inspected with narrow-band imaging; no residual adenomatous tissue was seen.
- Cold forceps biopsies of the scar were obtained to confirm the absence of residual adenoma.
- The remainder of the colon was normal.
No polyp was removed today.
Impression:
1. Healed ascending colon polypectomy scar without visible residual polyp; scar biopsied.
2. Otherwise normal colonoscopy.
Plan: Await pathology; the next surveillance interval depends on the biopsy result.
